source.locator: Seeds and regeneration; Obsidian export; corroborated by src/main.ts and src/export/obsidian.ts on same SHA

observation.observed_fact: The project documents regional map generation, renaming and notes, JSON persistence, and an Obsidian vault export. Static code connects rename/notes edits to browser save, serializes the world to JSON, reads JSON back, and emits site notes and world.json into a vault.
observation.interpretation: One existing alternative addresses an L1 preparation and handoff workflow. Static implementation evidence is stronger than a catalog promise, but does not prove deployed runtime correctness, WWN rules fidelity, user adoption or willingness to switch to HexCrawl.

operational_requirement.source_rule_ref: obs-WWN-BUILDER-20261110 (competitor workflow, not a game rule)
operational_requirement.normative_kind: non-normative product workflow; research interpretation only
operational_requirement.applicability: Optional transfer of a prepared WWN regional map and edited place notes into an external notes tool
operational_requirement.trigger_or_user_action: After renaming a prepared place and writing a note, export the map and place information for use in Obsidian.

inputs_and_units.place: one existing location named Old Port, renamed New Port
inputs_and_units.placement: retain the same position on the exported map

operational_requirement.product_operation: Transfer current edited map/place content together, so the user can find the place on the map, read its latest name/note and retain the source document for later continuation. The analyst chooses the eventual export design.
operational_requirement.expected_output: New Port appears at its original map location with the note Harbor closes at dusk; map and place notes remain mutually navigable.
constraints_and_exceptions: Source is software behavior, not a mandatory WWN rule.
The existing HX-BL-029 is proposed; this research does not authorize it or dictate bundled plugins/technical format.
External edits flowing back into the generator are not established; the included world.json is a snapshot, not evidence of Markdown round-trip sync.
HexCrawl current runtime support is unknown; do not label export absent without checking.

acceptance_cases.given: Existing Old Port, edited to New Port with note Harbor closes at dusk
acceptance_cases.when: Export the current prepared map and places
acceptance_cases.expected: Exported place title is New Port and the note is retained; no duplicate Old Port is created by the rename

acceptance_cases.given: New Port remains in the same map position
acceptance_cases.when: Open the exported map and select its place marker
acceptance_cases.expected: The corresponding New Port note is reachable at that position

acceptance_cases.given: The exported original source document snapshot with New Port and its note
acceptance_cases.when: Load that snapshot back into the generating tool without changing it externally
acceptance_cases.expected: The prepared map/place content is retained; this does not promise importing later external Markdown edits

operational_requirement.source_vs_product_interpretation: The competitor supplies an implemented transfer model. Cases express a user outcome for existing029; they are research examples, not a new WWN profile, detailed specification or release evidence.
unresolved_parameters: Whether users need one-way export or bidirectional synchronization

separated_conclusions.facts: Source implements save/edit/export paths and includes a standalone source snapshot.
separated_conclusions.inference: An existing alternative reduces the uniqueness of a proposed WWN-to-Obsidian workflow; proposal029 should define a concrete user advantage before implementation.
separated_conclusions.unknown: Hosted runtime, independent adoption, book fidelity, unmet need and switching probability
